correctness.rationale: Brownian covariance matrix is reconstructed from positive branch lengths and a common ultrametric height 55. Every possible four-out-of-five subset is inverted symbolically, with all resulting rational identities checked by an independent checker. A strictly positive denominator and a cubic with one positive root prove the exact switching law. The four-tip obstruction covers all sample sizes and both rooted binary tree shapes; the three-tip GLS coefficients are proved positive for every valid covariance, enabling covariance-decreasing replacement by the root singleton. Calculations are reproducible and limitations on unknown parameters are explicit.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Combining Ané’s optimization criterion with Ives’s additive covariance would define the same objective but does not in itself give the sharp minimum five tips, which requires a universal four-tip comparison and a five-tip construction. originality.rationale: The original part is the sharp five-tip minimum for a noise-induced change in optimal root-mean taxon subset and the explicit unique threshold. The known Brownian covariance, GLS criterion, noise-error covariance augmentation, and tree-based selection objective are excluded from the novelty claim. Source-level mathematical implication comparisons did not identify an established theorem covering the precise sharp threshold, though specialized general Gaussian experimental-design literature remains a residual originality risk.
residual_risks: Specialized Gaussian optimal subset/sensor selection or phylogenetic sampling theorems not located by title, parameter, equivalent mean-precision objective or broader-coverage searches might already imply this sharp threshold.
Published numerical design tables not indexed in the accessible repositories could incidentally contain equivalent five-tip examples.
Literature nonappearance does not certify absolute novelty; the result has only the indicated self-review.

value.rationale: Ané (2008) explicitly motivates selective taxon sampling to maximize precision of ancestral state inference; Ives et al. (2007) shows measurement uncertainty belongs in the phylogenetic GLS covariance. The new sharp minimum distinguishes models where optimal selected taxa are robust to measurement quality from the smallest case where they are not. The five-tip threshold uses a naturally constrained 4-of-5 selection with strict nonoverlapping optimal families, rather than a contrived index unconnected to a biological question; it is a reproducible counterexample useful for tree-aware experimental design.
